newsitem.title: UK: Thousands of Jews served in Hitler's army - report.
newsitem.headline: Thousands of Jews served in Hitler's army - report.

text.p: Thousands of soldiers of Jewish parentage served in Hitler's army during World War Two and fought for the Nazi leaders who ordered the extermination of Jews, the Daily Telegraph reported on Monday.

A study by Bryan Rigg, a history student now working at Cambridge University, showed Hitler knew dozens of his senior officers had Jewish origins and that he signed documents declaring them to be of German blood, the newspaper said.
Rigg, a 25-year-old American, interviewed hundreds of former soldiers and their families and examined army personnel files in the German federal government archives.
Field Marshal Erhard Milch, deputy to Luftwaffe chief Hermann Goering, was half Jewish, according to Rigg's study.
Goering, Hitler's chosen successor, knew Milch's background and falsified documents to cover up the Jewish link.
German law under the Nazis from 1935 barred anyone with a Jewish grandparent from becoming an officer.
But the German army personnel office in January 1944 knew of 77 "high-ranking officers of mixed Jewish race or married to a Jew".
All 77 had received a declaration from Hitler that they were of German blood.
